problem_description: Calculate the friction_coefficient between two crystalline slabs with surface asperities, where the box is in two dimensions with periodic boundary conditions along the sliding (x) direction and shrink-wrapped, non-periodic boundary conditions along the normal (y) direction. The 2D geometry must be explicitly enforced throughout the simulation to zero out z-velocities and forces. The system is constructed on a hexagonal lattice with lattice constant 0.9 inside a simulation box extending from x=0 to 50, y=0 to 22, and in the z direction from −0.25 to 0.25. Four atom types of equal mass 1.0 should be defined to distinguish slab atoms (type 1), asperity atoms (type 2 & 3), and fixed boundary atoms (type 4). A lower slab occupying the region y=0 to 7 and an upper slab occupying the region y=15 to 22 should be created, with rigid boundary layers are fixed at the bottom (y=0 to 1.1) and top (y = 20.9 to 22) of the simulation box by explicitly setting the forces on these boundary atoms to zero. Surface roughness should be introduced by creating hemispherical asperities of radius 8 on each slab, centered at (32, 7, 0) for the lower slab and (18, 15, 0) for the upper slab, retaining only the hemispherical portions facing the opposing surface. All atoms should interact via a Lennard–Jones potential with parameters ϵ=1.0, σ=1.0, and a cutoff radius of 2.5, using a neighbor list skin distance of 0.3 updated every five timesteps. Initial velocities corresponding to a temperature of 0.1 should be assigned to all mobile atoms, and the upper slab should be driven at a constant velocity of 1.0 along the x-direction. The equations of motion should be integrated using the NVE ensemble with a timestep of 0.0025. A velocity rescaling thermostat should be applied only to the mobile atoms and only to the non-sliding degrees of freedom to maintain the target temperature of 0.1. The simulation should run for 100,000 timesteps. Thermodynamic data and time-averaged friction outputs are logged every 1,000 steps. Atomic configurations are written to an XYZ file every 100 steps, while custom detailed trajectories are output every 500 steps for visualization and analysis. The friction coefficient should be calculated by summing the total force components on the upper slab in the x-direction (F_fric) and dividing by the normal force (F_norm), which is the total force components in the y-direction, calculating their absolute ratio, and continuously time-averaging these values.
